They are the equivalent of [API Routes](/docs/pages/building-your-application/routing/api-routes) inside the `pages` directory meaning you **do not** need to use API Routes and Route Handlers together. 26 27 ### Convention 28 29 Route Handlers are defined in a [`route.js|ts` file](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) inside the `app` directory: 30 31 ```ts filename="app/api/route.ts" switcher 32 export async function GET(request: Request) {} 33 ``` 34 35 ```js filename="app/api/route.js" switcher 36 export async function GET(request) {} 37 ``` 38 39 Route Handlers can be nested anywhere inside the `app` directory, similar to `page.js` and `layout.js`. But there **cannot** be a `route.js` file at the same route segment level as `page.js`. 40 41 ### Supported HTTP Methods 42 43 The following [HTTP methods](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods) are supported: `GET`, `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `HEAD`, and `OPTIONS`. If an unsupported method is called, Next.js will return a `405 Method Not Allowed` response. 44 45 ### Extended `NextRequest` and `NextResponse` APIs 46 47 In addition to supporting the native [Request](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Request) and [Response](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/Response) APIs, Next.js extends them with [`NextRequest`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-request) and [`NextResponse`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-response) to provide convenient helpers for advanced use cases. 48 49 ### Caching 50 51 Route Handlers are not cached by default. You can, however, opt into caching for `GET` methods. Other supported HTTP methods are **not** cached. To cache a `GET` method, use a [route config option](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic) such as `export const dynamic = 'force-static'` in your Route Handler file. 52 53 ```ts filename="app/items/route.ts" switcher 54 export const dynamic = 'force-static' 55 56 export async function GET() { 57 const res = await fetch('https://data.mongodb-api.com/...', { 58 headers: { 59 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 60 'API-Key': process.env.DATA_API_KEY, 61 }, 62 }) 63 const data = await res.json() 64 65 return Response.json({ data }) 66 } 67 ``` 68 69 ```js filename="app/items/route.js" switcher 70 export const dynamic = 'force-static' 71 72 export async function GET() { 73 const res = await fetch('https://data.mongodb-api.com/...', { 74 headers: { 75 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 76 'API-Key': process.env.DATA_API_KEY, 77 }, 78 }) 79 const data = await res.json() 80 81 return Response.json({ data }) 82 } 83 ``` 84 85 > **Good to know**: Other supported HTTP methods are **not** cached, even if they are placed alongside a `GET` method that is cached, in the same file. 86 87 #### With Cache Components 88 89 When [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) is enabled, `GET` Route Handlers follow the same model as normal UI routes in your application. They run at request time by default, can be prerendered when they don't access uncached or runtime data, and you can use `use cache` to include uncached data in the static response. 90 91 **Static example** - doesn't access uncached or runtime data, so it will be prerendered at build time: 92 93 ```tsx filename="app/api/project-info/route.ts" 94 export async function GET() { 95 return Response.json({ 96 projectName: 'Next.js', 97 }) 98 } 99 ``` 100 101 **Dynamic example** - accesses non-deterministic operations. During the build, prerendering stops when `Math.random()` is called, deferring to request-time rendering: 102 103 ```tsx filename="app/api/random-number/route.ts" 104 export async function GET() { 105 return Response.json({ 106 randomNumber: Math.random(), 107 }) 108 } 109 ``` 110 111 **Runtime data example** - accesses request-specific data. Hello, Next.js!

168 } 169 170 // Conflict 171 // `app/route.ts` 172 export async function POST(request: Request) {} 173 ``` 174 175 ```js filename="app/page.js" switcher 176 export default function Page() { 177 return

Hello, Next.js!

178 } 179 180 // Conflict 181 // `app/route.js` 182 export async function POST(request) {} 183 ``` 184 185 Read more about how Route Handlers [complement your frontend application](/docs/app/guides/backend-for-frontend), or explore the Route Handlers [API Reference](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route). 186 187 ### Route Context Helper 188 189 In TypeScript, you can type the `context` parameter for Route Handlers with the globally available [`RouteContext`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route#route-context-helper) helper: 190 191 ```ts filename="app/users/[id]/route.ts" switcher 192 import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server' 193 194 export async function GET(_req: NextRequest, ctx: RouteContext<'/users/[id]'>) { 195 const { id } = await ctx.params 196 return Response.json({ id }) 197 } 198 ``` 199 200 > **Good to know** 201 > 202 > - Types are generated during `next dev`, `next build` or `next typegen`.

3  	description: API reference for the generateStaticParams function.
4  	---
5  	
6  	The `generateStaticParams` function can be used in combination with [dynamic route segments](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) to [**statically generate**](/docs/app/glossary#prerendering) routes at build time instead of on-demand at request time.
7  	
8  	`generateStaticParams` can be used with:
9  	
10 	- [Pages](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) (`page.tsx`/`page.js`)
11 	- [Layouts](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout) (`layout.tsx`/`layout.js`)
12 	- [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) (`route.ts`/`route.js`)
13 	
14 	```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
15 	// Return a list of `params` to populate the [slug] dynamic segment
16 	export async function generateStaticParams() {
17 	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
18 	
19 	  return posts.map((post) => ({
20 	    slug: post.slug,
21 	  }))
22 	}
23 	
24 	// Multiple versions of this page will be statically generated
25 	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
26 	export default async function Page({
27 	  params,
28 	}: {
29 	  params: Promise<{ slug: string }>
30 	}) {
31 	  const { slug } = await params
32 	  // ...
33 	}
34 	```
35 	
36 	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
37 	// Return a list of `params` to populate the [slug] dynamic segment
38 	export async function generateStaticParams() {
39 	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
40 	
41 	  return posts.map((post) => ({
42 	    slug: post.slug,
43 	  }))
44 	}
45 	
46 	// Multiple versions of this page will be statically generated
47 	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
48 	export default async function Page({ params }) {
49 	  const { slug } = await params
50 	  // ...
51 	}
52 	```
53 	
54 	> **Good to know**:
55 	>
56 	> - You can use the [`dynamicParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/dynamicParams) segment config option to control what happens when a dynamic segment is visited that was not generated with `generateStaticParams`.
57 	> - You must return [an empty array from `generateStaticParams`](#all-paths-at-runtime) or utilize [`export const dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic) in order to revalidate (ISR) [paths at runtime](#all-paths-at-runtime).
58 	> - During `next dev`, `generateStaticParams` will be called when you navigate to a route.
59 	> - During `next build`, `generateStaticParams` runs before the corresponding Layouts or Pages are generated.
60 	> - During revalidation (ISR), `generateStaticParams` will not be called again.
61 	> - `generateStaticParams` replaces the [`getStaticPaths`](/docs/pages/api-reference/functions/get-static-paths) function in the Pages Router.
62 	
63 	## Parameters
64 	
65 	`options.params` (optional)
66 	
67 	If multiple dynamic segments in a route use `generateStaticParams`, the child `generateStaticParams` function is executed once for each set of `params` the parent generates.
68 	
69 	The `params` object contains the populated `params` from the parent `generateStaticParams`, which can be used to [generate the `params` in a child segment](#multiple-dynamic-segments-in-a-route).
70 	
71 	## Returns
72 	
73 	`generateStaticParams` should return an array of objects where each object represents the populated dynamic segments of a single route.
74 	
75 	- Each property in the object is a dynamic segment to be filled in for the route.
76 	- The properties name is the segment's name, and the properties value is what that segment should be filled in with.
77

80 	| `/product/[id]`                  | `{ id: string }[]`                        |
81 	| `/products/[category]/[product]` | `{ category: string, product: string }[]` |
82 	| `/products/[...slug]`            | `{ slug: string[] }[]`                    |
83

103	}
104	```
